headline: PLS.AX hits hard with a 5.5% drop today as lithium woes continue, while last night's NASDAQ surge kept US holdings buoyant — and the RBA rate cut hopes have all but evaporated until 2027.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara copped a 5.5% hit today in a tough session for ASX lithium stocks broadly. The sector is under pressure from ongoing weak lithium prices and balance sheet concerns flagged across the industry — it's not a Pilbara-specific crisis, but the whole lithium space is hurting right now. Long-term story is intact if you believe in the EV transition, but it's a bumpy ride.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets pulled back 1.2% today on the ASX. Broader global risk sentiment and a stronger USD weigh on this ETF, which holds companies across China, India, Taiwan and other developing markets. No single dramatic catalyst — just routine volatility in a sector that swings more than developed markets.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google bounced a solid 2.5% last night on the NASDAQ as tech broadly rallied after Trump issued an upbeat economic outlook, boosting AI and big tech names. GOOG is now up 18.7% on your total investment — a strong performer in the portfolio.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two nudged up 1.3% last night, riding the general tech and gaming sector tailwind. No specific news catalyst, but the stock continues to recover well — up 12.7% overall on your investment.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dipped about 1% last night despite launching a $2.5 billion 'Frontier Company' enterprise AI venture. The market shrugged — investors may be cautious after MSFT's big run-up, and the stock remains down 12.7% on your total investment. The AI push is a long-term positive, but the market wants to see it translate to earnings.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF ticked up a modest 0.24% today, steady as AI sentiment remains constructive globally. VanEck also launched a competing AI ETF in Australia today, showing the sector is attracting more attention — not a threat to GXAI, just a sign the space is growing.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS edged up 0.26% today, tracking the positive lead from last night's US session. The S&P 500 rose 0.7% and NASDAQ gained 1.1% last night — VTS absorbs that broadly and is up 3.7% on your overall investment.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was essentially flat today, down just 0.09%. As a diversified fund across global and Aussie shares, bonds and property, it absorbs daily noise well. Sitting slightly above your purchase price overall — doing exactly what it's designed to do.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — down 5.5% today, but hold your nerve
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped sharply today and is now down 27.9% on your total investment. That stings, but this is sector-wide lithium weakness, not a Pilbara-specific blow-up. UBS actually named Pilbara among its top lithium picks with a bullish long-term outlook this week. If you believe EVs are the future (and most analysts do), the long-term case is still intact. This is a long-term hold — sit tight unless you want to top up at these levels.

watch_today.title: RBA rate cut off the table until 2027 — what it means for you
watch_today.detail: Multiple economists now say there'll be no RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) interest rate cuts until at least 2027, and a fourth rate RISE is still on the table. That means higher mortgage costs continue longer, consumer spending stays squeezed, and property prices face headwinds. For your portfolio, it's a mild headwind for Aussie shares generally but doesn't change the long-term case for your ETFs.

watch_today.title: MSFT — down on your investment, new AI bet is a long-term play
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is down 12.7% on your total investment and slipped another 1% last night. The company just launched a $2.5 billion enterprise AI business, doubling down on AI for large companies. One analyst piece flags MSFT is down 30% from highs but still posting record earnings — that's actually a compelling long-term entry point. No reason to sell; the AI story is exactly why you'd hold this for the long haul.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI regulation wave building globally
watch_today.detail: Illinois just signed a landmark AI regulation bill, Thailand is drafting AI laws, and the UN Secretary-General called for global AI regulation today. More regulation could slow AI adoption short-term but tends to legitimise the sector long-term. Your GXAI.AX ETF is down 11% overall but steady today. Hold for the long-term AI theme.

watch_today.title: DeepSeek V4 launches — China's AI challenge to US tech is real
watch_today.detail: China's DeepSeek has released its V4 model, competing directly with ChatGPT, Claude, and Google's Gemini. This is worth watching because it pressures the pricing power of US AI companies and could shake up the competitive landscape for GOOG and MSFT. Not an immediate sell signal — both are diversified businesses — but worth keeping an eye on as the AI arms race intensifies.

watch_today.title: GOOG — strong night, up 18.7% overall
watch_today.detail: Google jumped 2.5% last night and is your best-performing position overall at +18.7%. No specific news drove it — it rode the broader tech rally. Nothing to do here but enjoy it. Classic long-term hold.

world.summary: A deadly landslide in India, Trump renewing military threats against Iran, European recession warnings, and a record year for global LNG trade dominated world news today.

stories.title: Major landslide hits Kerala tunnel construction site — multiple feared trapped
stories.why_it_matters: A serious landslide struck a tunnel construction site in Wayanad, Kerala in southern India today, with multiple workers feared trapped under debris. Rescue operations are underway. Wayanad is a mountainous region prone to landslides — it suffered a devastating slide in 2024 that killed over 200 people. This is a developing story with the human toll still unknown.

stories.title: Trump renews threat of military action against Iran
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump has again threatened to 'finish the job' with military force against Iran if nuclear diplomacy fails, escalating tensions in the Middle East. This follows ongoing US-Iran nuclear talks that have stalled. A military strike on Iran would likely send oil prices sharply higher — crude is already up 1.5% to $69.60/barrel last night — and could destabilise global energy markets. Worth watching closely given your VTS.AX and broader global exposure.

stories.title: Europe faces recession risk if US market sell-off and new Middle East war hit simultaneously
stories.why_it_matters: Europe's financial rescue fund (the ESM — think of it as the eurozone's emergency bank) has warned that if a US stock market sell-off coincides with a new Middle East war, the eurozone could tip into recession. Europe's economy is already fragile, with high energy costs and sluggish growth. For an Australian investor, a European recession would drag on global growth and emerging markets, affecting your VGE.AX and VDHG.AX holdings.

stories.title: Global LNG trade hit a record in 2025, but Middle East conflict clouds the outlook
stories.why_it_matters: The International Gas Union (IGU) says global trade in liquefied natural gas (LNG — basically natural gas chilled into liquid so it can be shipped) hit a new record in 2025. That's good news for Australian LNG exporters. However, the IGU warns that an escalation of Middle East conflict could disrupt shipping routes and supply chains, potentially causing energy price spikes globally. Australia is one of the world's biggest LNG exporters, so this has direct economic relevance.

stories.title: FIFA World Cup 2026: Folarin Balogun — the 'accidental American' at the centre of soccer politics
stories.why_it_matters: Folarin Balogun is one of the most talked-about players at the FIFA World Cup — born in the US, raised in England, he represents the US men's team. His story touches on the messy politics of international football eligibility and national identity in a World Cup hosted on US soil for the first time. With the tournament in full swing, expect Balogun's dual-identity story to keep making headlines.

markets.summary: Last night the NASDAQ surged 1.1% and the S&P 500 gained 0.7% after Trump struck an upbeat economic tone, lifting AI and tech stocks. The ASX 200 gave back 0.3% today. Oil jumped 1.5% to $69.60 on Middle East tensions, while gold eased slightly. The Aussie dollar is steady at 69.4 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Soft session on the ASX today — modest 0.3% dip, with lithium and emerging market ETFs among the drags.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session: solid gain driven by Trump's bullish economic commentary and a tech rally.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night's session: tech and AI stocks bounced strongly, the best performer of the major indices.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil spiked 1.5% last night as Trump's renewed Iran military threats spooked energy markets.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold eased slightly as risk appetite improved on the back of the US equity rally.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar is essentially flat — no major moves today, sitting comfortably near 69.4 US cents.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is grim news on interest rates — economists are now saying rate cuts are off the table until 2027 at the earliest, with some even flagging a fourth rate hike. The RBA is under fire for failing to get on top of inflation.

stories.title: No rate cuts until 2027 — and a fourth rate rise is on the table, economists warn
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's leading economists have all but ruled out RBA interest rate cuts until 2027, with some warning a fourth rate increase is still possible if inflation stays sticky. That means Australians with mortgages face at least another 18 months of high repayments. For everyday Aussies, it means less money in their pockets and continued pressure on household budgets. For investors, it's a headwind for consumer-facing ASX companies and property values.

stories.title: 'The RBA failed': Sky News calls out Australia's inflation problem
stories.why_it_matters: Sky News has run a scathing segment arguing the Reserve Bank of Australia 'failed' in its primary job of keeping inflation in check. The criticism centres on the RBA moving too slowly to raise rates when inflation first surged, leaving Australia with a longer and more painful inflation fight than comparable countries like Canada and the US. It adds political heat to the RBA and keeps rate policy front of mind heading into 2027.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the theme of the day globally — Illinois signed a landmark bill, Thailand drafted one, and the UN Secretary-General is calling for worldwide rules. Meanwhile, China's DeepSeek released V4 to take on the big Western AI models.

stories.title: Illinois Governor Pritzker signs landmark AI regulation bill
stories.why_it_matters: Illinois has become one of the first US states to pass a comprehensive AI regulation law, signed by Governor Pritzker. The bill is designed to reduce risks from AI systems — think things like algorithmic discrimination in hiring or lending. It mirrors elements of Europe's AI Act. This is significant because state-level AI laws in the US could eventually push Congress toward a national framework, which would directly affect how companies like Google and Microsoft deploy their AI products.

stories.title: UN Secretary-General calls for global AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has called on world leaders to establish binding international regulations for artificial intelligence, warning that without global rules, AI risks becoming ungovernable. He pointed to risks ranging from AI-generated misinformation to autonomous weapons. A global regulatory push would affect every major tech company — but could also legitimise and stabilise the sector for long-term investors.

stories.title: DeepSeek V4 launches — China takes on ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini
stories.why_it_matters: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek has released its V4 model, positioning it as a direct rival to OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Google's Gemini. DeepSeek has a track record of releasing powerful models at a fraction of the cost of Western competitors. V4 is reportedly competitive on most benchmarks. This matters for investors in Google (GOOG) and Microsoft (MSFT) — it means the AI race is intensifying and pricing power for AI tools could be squeezed by cheap Chinese alternatives.

stories.title: Will Albanese let unions put the brakes on AI in Australia?
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR is questioning whether PM Albanese will allow union pressure to slow Australia's adoption of AI in the workplace. Australian unions, particularly in industries like media, education, and public services, are pushing for strict rules on how AI can replace workers. The tension is between protecting jobs now versus Australia keeping pace with global AI adoption. This debate will shape how quickly Australian businesses can deploy AI tools — and could affect productivity growth.

sport.summary: Big NRL TV rights news today — a $5.3 billion mega-deal with Foxtel, Nine, and Sky NZ was announced. Wimbledon continues with Osaka in the spotlight and Aussie doubles pairs doing well. AFL's top-of-the-table clash looms on Thursday.

stories.title: $5.3 billion NRL TV rights mega-deal locked in with Foxtel, Nine, and Sky NZ
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL has announced a massive $5.3 billion TV rights deal with Foxtel (Kayo), Nine Network, and Sky New Zealand. This is one of the biggest sports media deals in Australian history and secures the NRL's broadcast future for years ahead. Kayo subscribers have been nervous about rising costs — executives moved quickly to hose down concerns, but expect your Kayo bill to be under pressure. The deal confirms the NRL as a premium content asset.

stories.title: Naomi Osaka surges at Wimbledon — could a first grass title be next?
stories.why_it_matters: Naomi Osaka, once the world's number one player, is on a remarkable Wimbledon run that has the tennis world talking about whether she can claim her first ever grass court Grand Slam title. Aryna Sabalenka — who Osaka beat — reportedly told reporters she planned to 'get completely drunk' after the loss. Meanwhile, Filipino-American Alex Eala is being hailed as a national icon in the Philippines despite her Wimbledon exit, drawing comparisons to boxing legend Manny Pacquiao.

stories.title: Aussie doubles pairs Hunter and Polmans keeping the flag flying at Wimbledon
stories.why_it_matters: Australian doubles pairs John-Patrick Smith/Hunter and Marc Polmans are progressing well at Wimbledon 2026, keeping Australian tennis representation alive deep in the draw. Doubles doesn't get the headlines but it's a solid result for Australian tennis depth.

stories.title: Gold Coast Suns call in NRL club to help fix a losing streak
stories.why_it_matters: In a creative move, the Gold Coast Suns AFL club has brought in an NRL club to help address their losing streak — likely for specialist sports science, conditioning, or culture work. The Suns have been struggling with consistency and are clearly thinking outside the box. A local Gold Coast story worth following — the Suns are your home team!

stories.title: AFL's top-two clash: Sydney Swans v GWS Giants on Thursday night
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Swans and GWS Giants — the AFL's top two sides — face off in a mouth-watering Thursday night blockbuster. The Swans are reportedly planning to use the Giants' own game plan against them, having studied their 'blueprint' closely. Both clubs' coaches previewed the game as a genuine top-of-the-ladder statement match. If you follow footy, this is must-watch TV.
